NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI computing value chain as a fabless semiconductor designer, critically dependent on TSMC for cutting-edge chip fabrication and on HBM memory suppliers like Micron and SK Hynix for GPU performance. On the demand side, NVIDIA's revenue is heavily concentrated among a small number of hyperscale cloud providers and AI-native companies racing to build out GPU infrastructure, giving it extraordinary pricing power but also meaningful customer concentration risk.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the premium end of the consumer electronics value chain, acting as a powerful orchestrator that outsources chip fabrication primarily to TSMC and display production to Samsung/LG while maintaining tight design control over its proprietary silicon and software ecosystem. On the downstream side, Apple's revenue is driven by a vast global consumer base with key channel dependencies on telecom carriers and digital platform partners, most notably Google's search revenue-sharing agreement which materially supports Apple's high-margin Services segment.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron occupies a critical middle position in the semiconductor value chain as one of only three global suppliers of DRAM (alongside Samsung and SK Hynix) and a major NAND flash producer, making it highly dependent on a concentrated group of capital equipment vendors for its fab buildout and technology transitions. Its customer base spans hyperscale cloud providers, mobile OEMs, and AI accelerator makers, with surging demand for High Bandwidth Memory from NVIDIA positioning Micron as a key enabler of the AI infrastructure buildout.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM occupies a unique, asset-light position at the top of the semiconductor IP stack, generating royalty and licensing revenue by providing foundational CPU, GPU, and system IP to virtually every major chip designer across mobile, data center, automotive, and IoT markets. As a pure IP licensor, ARM has minimal physical upstream dependencies but is critically reliant on EDA toolchain providers like Cadence and Synopsys, while its downstream customer concentration—particularly Apple (~25% of royalties) and Qualcomm—represents a meaningful revenue risk given their outsized share of ARM-based silicon shipments.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology is a fabless semiconductor company positioned in the middle of the data infrastructure supply chain, relying heavily on TSMC for advanced node manufacturing and EDA vendors like Cadence and Synopsys for chip design. It primarily serves hyperscalers, cloud providers, and networking OEMs with custom ASICs, Ethernet solutions, and storage controllers, making it a critical enabler of AI and data center infrastructure buildout.
